newsitem.title: USA: OfficeMax seen poised for growth.
newsitem.headline: OfficeMax seen poised for growth.

text.p: OfficeMax Inc appeared left in the lurch early this month when the two other office supply superstores, Office Depot Inc and Staples Inc, announced plans to merge.
But analysts say nimble expansion, while the new-born giant lumbers to life, should allow OfficeMax to grow unfettered for the next few years.

"There is still a lot of market share they can penetrate before OfficeMax and the new entity start having to hit each other over the head," said Donald Spindel, an analyst with A.G. Edwards & Sons Inc. "Both stores have ample opportunity to take market share from small mom and pop stores and smaller regional chains."
OfficeMax said Tuesday it will accelerate its store expansion plans for the balance of fiscal 1996 by opening a total of 95 to 100 superstores as well as dramatically increasing next year's openings.
It said it plans to open about 125 to 150 stores next year, up from the previously announced plan of 80 for both years.
"It makes perfect sense," said Mark Mandel, an analyst for The Chicago Corp. "They have the capital and the strategic opportunity. It was really a no-brainer."
Before the merger, Office Depot and Staples collectively planned to open about 200 stores in 1997. Now they're planning to open 120 but are closing up to 70, Mendel noted.

"OfficeMax was going to have to face two aggressively growing companies; now they have to face one larger company that for the next two years will have to focus more on integration than expansion," Mandel said.

Spindel said the office superstore market is still open enough to allow both entities to grow for several years without impinging on each other. "There's no reason to wage a price war with each other when there's still ample opportunity to take business from the other weaker stores that are out there," Spindel said. "They won't have to start bloodying each other's noses for at least several years."
Spindel said OfficeMax should also stay healthy via its expanded ancillary services that differentiate it from the competition.
He cited CopyMax, OfficeMax's pay-for-print store-within-a-store operation. The company is scheduled to have 425 CopyMax locations by end of this year.
FurnitureMax, the company's expanded office furniture store-within-a-store, is another example, Spindel said. The company is expected to have 65 such locations by year's end.
"They're devoting more time and resources to these two types of operations than Staples/Office Depot," Spindel said.
Mandel said OfficeMax needs to keep looking for opportunities in other countries.
"They have a joint venture in Mexico and plan to have 50 stores there in the next three to five years," Mendel said. "And they've talked about Asia, which would seem to make sense."
